overview: Both are chemical messengers, but they differ in how far they travel and how fast they act.
genZNote: Hormone: a slow-burn email sent through the bloodstream. Neurotransmitter: an instant text across a tiny gap.

aspects.label: Distance Travelled
aspects.valueA: Travels through the bloodstream to often distant target organs.
aspects.valueB: Travels across a tiny synaptic gap to an adjacent neuron or effector cell.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Insulin, adrenaline (as a hormone from the adrenal medulla).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Adrenaline is a great crossover example — it acts as a hormone when released from the adrenal medulla into the blood, and as a neurotransmitter at some synapses.
overlay.memoryTrick: Hormone = long-distance, slow. Neurotransmitter = short-distance, fast.
overlay.commonMisconception: Neurotransmitters are not exclusive to the brain — they act throughout the peripheral nervous system too, including at neuromuscular junctions.
